claimBoundary: This file enumerates normal-case source-derived route and component canonicalization outcomes. The separately recorded partial synthetic browser slices do not execute every role/route/viewport/state cell, do not create owner aesthetic acceptance, and are not merge, staging, Sites, or production authority.

dimensionCorrection.previousProblem: The prior schema treated customer, accountant, and group-lead as UserRole values and attached every profile to every route without an expected outcome.
dimensionCorrection.currentModel: Access profiles combine authentication, the persisted role, account status, and customer/accountant relationship flags because the route guard uses all of those inputs.

normalCaseAssumptions: guest has neither an access token nor a refresh token.
authenticated profiles have a valid token and the exact active authoritative identity shown in accessProfiles.
/api/auth/me authority lookup is ready when an access-specific guard needs it.

Parameterized route IDs are syntactically valid; component/API-level ownership and object authorization are outside this route-level matrix except for the explicitly listed AdminView canonicalization outcomes.

acceptanceDimensions.status: requirements-not-expanded; limited synthetic browser slices are recorded separately and do not satisfy full-matrix acceptance

limitations: Synthetic local browser evidence only; it does not cover all nine profiles or all thirty routes.
It does not expand or pass the required viewport, state, interaction, or environment dimensions.
This is a focused visual and accessibility recovery slice, not a role-by-route execution of the full matrix.
The rendered evidence is local and synthetic; no screenshot asset or live deployment is stored or implied.
A subsequent local P1 change exists outside this source commit; its validation is pending, so this receipt makes no current-working-tree product claim.

accessOutcomeDefinitions.render-route: The guard calls next() for the stated normal-case profile.
accessOutcomeDefinitions.redirect-login: The authenticated route stores a safe intended route and redirects to the named login route.
accessOutcomeDefinitions.redirect-home: An authenticated visit to /login redirects to /.
accessOutcomeDefinitions.redirect-canonical: The router record redirects to its named canonical route; the target guard still applies.
accessOutcomeDefinitions.redirect-forbidden-recovery: An authoritative access-specific denial redirects with the forbidden recovery outcome.
accessOutcomeDefinitions.redirect-component-canonical: The router permits the route, then the named component canonicalizes a denied subsection to the stated target; this is neither a router-record redirect nor a forbidden recovery.

accessProfiles.guardNote: The current route guard has no owner flag; this profile is intentionally access-equivalent to member.

nonProfileEdgeConditions.condition: Authentication refresh/check is temporarily unavailable on /login or any requiresAuth route.
An access-specific /api/auth/me probe is unavailable, malformed, non-authoritative, or times out.
An authoritative identity is inactive on a requiresMarketAccess or requiresOwnerAccess route.
